chunks: I mentioned the voice in his presence, so he said: 'Indeed, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to recite, and sometimes a passer-by would pass by him and would be struck unconscious from the beauty of his voice. And verily, the Imam — if he were to manifest anything of that, the people would not be able to bear its beauty.'

I said: 'And did not the Messenger of God (blessings of God upon him and his family) lead the people in prayer while raising his voice with the Quran?' So he said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of God (blessings of God upon him and his family) used to impose upon the people behind him only what they could endure.'

key_terms.حُسْنُ الصَّوْتِ: Beauty of the voice — a quality associated with the Imams' recitation of Quran that surpasses ordinary human vocal beauty
key_terms.صَعِقَ: To be struck unconscious or overwhelmed — used in the Quran (39:68) for the blast that strikes all unconscious on the Day of Resurrection; here used for swooning from the beauty of the Imam's recitation
key_terms.يُطِيقُونَ: That which they can endure/bear — referring to the people's capacity to withstand the spiritual intensity of the Prophet's recitation

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn recite the Quran quietly and what happened to passers-by who heard him?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain leading to Abu al-Hasan (as), reveals that the Imams possess a divine quality in their Quranic recitation so beautiful that it overwhelms human perception. Imam Zayn al-Abidin (as) would sometimes render passing strangers unconscious by the sheer beauty of his voice. The Prophet (saww) likewise constrained his public recitation to what the congregation could spiritually and physically bear — a merciful concession to human capacity. The hadith reflects the Shia belief that the Imams carry latent divine gifts that, if fully manifested, would surpass what ordinary human beings can withstand.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Hasan Bin Shamoun who said, ‘Ali Bin Muhammad Al Nowfaly narrated to me, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said: ‘The (good) voice was mentioned in his<sup>asws</sup> presence. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> used to recite. So sometimes a passer-by would pause (in order to listen), and he would shriek from the beauty of his<sup>asws</sup> voice, and that the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, if he<sup>as</sup> were to manifest anything from that, the people would not be able to bear the beauty of his<sup>asws</sup> voice’.

I said, ‘And why didn’t Rasool-Allahsaww raise hissaww voice with the Quran (recitation) when hesaww prayed Salāt with (leading) the people?’ So heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww used to only load upon the people – following himsaww what they could endure’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Hassan ibn Shammun who has that narrated to him Ali ibn Muhammad al- Nawfali from abu al-Hassan (a.s.) who has said the following: “Once accents and voices were mentioned before abu al- Hassan (a.s.) and he said, ‘Once Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) was reading and someone passing by suffered a shock due to the beauty of his voice. If the Imam were to manifest such reading people could not bear its beauty.’

I (the narrator) then said, ‘The Messenger of Allah during his prayer would not raise his voice in reading the Holy Quran.’ The Imam said, ‘The Messenger of Allah would make people behind him do only what they could tolerate.’”
